newsitem.title: USA: Denbury expects to salvage blown-out well.
newsitem.headline: Denbury expects to salvage blown-out well.

text.p: Crews planned to pump drilling mud down the wellbore of a natural gas well burning out of control in a coastal Louisiana marsh to extinguish the blaze, a spokesman with well operator Denbury Resources Inc said Tuesday.

Crews from International Well Control should have the fire, which was being fueled by about 20 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of natural gas, under control "in the next day or two," said Phil Rykhoek, Denbury's chief financial officer.

Once the fire is extinguished and the well capped, Dallas-based Denbury expects to salvage a well that had been expected to flow at 5 mmcfd, Ryhoek said. No other production from nearby wells was affected by the blowout, he said.
"It will probably be tomorrow before they can actually get on (the rig)," he said. "Some equipment failed, and we think it may have been the packer, but we're not sure."

Two workers were killed and two others missing following the overnight explosion and fire on the rig, which was located in a marsh in St. Martin Parish about 40 miles southwest of Baton Rouge, La., the company said.
Eighteen other workers were evacuated after the well blew out, sending flames shooting 200 feet into the air
Denbury produces an average 13,000 to 13,500 barrels per day of oil and equivalent, and expected no material impact of lost production from the Louisiana well, Ryhoek said.
